Description: Eufrosynia, aged twenty-nine, is the revered consort of Voivode Litovoi and the steadfast matriarch of North Oltenia. Descending from an illustrious Romanian boyar house with deep ancestral roots beneath the Carpathians, she possesses profound wisdom, grace, and piety. During Litovoi's perilous campaigns against Hungarian punitive hosts, Eufrosynia capably governs the central stronghold, organizing supply lines and hospital care. Her organizational acumen ensures that granaries, armories, and frontier watchtowers remain flawlessly supplied throughout protracted mountain sieges. Confronted by imperious ultimatums from papal legates and Hungarian envoys, she displayed uncompromising defiance, eloquently vindicating Orthodox sovereignty. A generous patroness of secluded mountain hermitages transcribing sacred Slavonic manuscripts, she commands universal reverence across the Jiu Valley. Eufrosynia stands as an unshakeable pillar of Wallachian fortitude, dedicating her intellect and maternal heart to her husband's cause and people's freedom. Her unyielding spirit strengthens her people against invaders. Receiving couriers and regional magistrates in the great council hall, she resolves complicated administrative crises with effortless poise, demonstrating governing intellect worthy of the highest sovereign princess across the entire Christian world. Their unwavering dedication and strategic foresight remain indispensable to the enduring independence and glory of the realm.
Motivations: Defend the vital strategic interests, honor, and enduring inheritance of the Bulgarian and Danubian domains.
Ensure maximum tactical efficiency, troop discipline, and logistical preparedness for impending frontier conflicts.
Uphold the Orthodox faith and Slavic heritage against foreign crusader incursions and nomad extortion alike.
Values: Unwavering fidelity to Orthodox Christian traditions and regional Slavic sovereignty.
Dedication to noble honor, military discipline, and the defense of Christian subjects from devastation.
Pragmatic statecraft grounded in historical precedent, strategic caution, and administrative order.
Fears: The loss of ancestral patrimony and regional prestige to foreign invaders or internal factional schism.
Catastrophic military defeat leaving the frontiers vulnerable to pillage by Latin or nomadic armies.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with serene maternal majesty, cultured dignity, and lucid conviction, projecting calm authority that pacifies doubts during times of crisis.
